## 1. Purpose

This procedure describes the operation, calibration, and maintenance of
the Turner Designs Trilogy Laboratory Fluorometer, a compact,
multifunctional instrument used for fluorescence, absorbance, and
turbidity measurements with interchangeable snap-in optical modules. The
Trilogy is the primary instrument in the EA Program laboratory for
chlorophyll *a* determination and turbidity analysis of water samples.


## 2. Scope

- **Applies to:** Turner Designs Trilogy Laboratory Fluorometer equipped
  with fluorescence, absorbance, and turbidity optical modules
- **Does not apply to:** Field fluorometers, in-vivo chlorophyll
  measurements with multiprobes (see
  [SOP-F200](../field_sops/SOP-F200-eureka-manta2.qmd)), or benchtop
  spectrophotometers (Hach DR3900; see
  [SOP-L303](SOP-L303-hach-colorimetric.qmd))
- **Location:** EA Program laboratory, SGM 133


## 3. Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve SOP, ensure calibration standards are current |
| Lab Manager       | Maintain optical modules, replace light sources as needed |
| Trained Personnel | Follow this SOP, report malfunctions        |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use    |


## 4. Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Chemical:** Chlorophyll extraction uses 90% acetone, which is
  flammable and an irritant. Handle in the fume hood. Acidification
  with HCl (0.1 N) is required for EPA 445.0. See
  [SOP-L003](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd).
- **Physical:** Glass test tubes used for extracted chlorophyll
  measurements can break. Handle with care.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses
- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Nitrile gloves (especially when handling acetone or standards)

### Emergency Procedures

For acetone spills, extinguish all ignition sources, ventilate the area,
and clean up per
[SOP-L003 Hazardous Materials Handling](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd).
For skin or eye contact with acetone or acid, flush with water for at
least 15 minutes.


## 5. Equipment and Materials

### Equipment

| Item                          | Notes                                     |
|:------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|
| Turner Designs Trilogy Fluorometer | With color touch screen               |
| Fluorescence optical module(s) | Application-specific (e.g., chlorophyll *a*, Rhodamine WT) |
| Absorbance optical module     | With interchangeable filter paddles (560/10, 600/10, 750/10 nm) |
| Turbidity optical module      | Infrared LED at 850 nm (ISO 7027)         |
| Solid secondary standard      | For verifying instrument stability        |
| Printer or PC connection      | For data export (USB or serial)           |

### Consumables

| Item                          | Notes                                     |
|:------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|
| Methacrylate cuvettes (10 x 10 mm) | Minimum 2 mL volume; for ammonium and general fluorescence |
| Polystyrene cuvettes (10 x 10 mm) | For turbidity measurements              |
| Glass cuvettes (10 x 10 mm)  | Minimum 1.5 mL volume; for absorbance     |
| Glass test tubes (12 x 35 mm) | For extracted chlorophyll measurements    |

### Reagents and Standards

| Item                          | Notes                                     |
|:------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|
| Chlorophyll *a* standard      | Pure chlorophyll *a* in 90% acetone; Turner Designs or equivalent |
| Rhodamine WT standard         | If using Rhodamine fluorescence module    |
| 90% acetone (reagent grade)   | For chlorophyll extraction solvent         |
| 0.1 N HCl                    | For acidification step (EPA 445.0)        |
| Formazine turbidity standards | 4,000 NTU primary standard; valid for 4 weeks after preparation |
| Ultrapure water               | For blanks                                |


## 6. Procedure

### 6.1 Startup

1. Turn on the Trilogy using the power switch on the back of the
   instrument
2. Allow the instrument to warm up for approximately 10 minutes before
   taking measurements
3. Connect the Trilogy to a printer or PC if data export is needed

### 6.2 Installing an Optical Module

1. Select the appropriate optical module for the analysis:
   - **Fluorescence module** for chlorophyll *a*, Rhodamine WT, or other
     fluorescent analytes
   - **Absorbance module** for colorimetric assays
   - **Turbidity module** for nephelometric turbidity measurements
2. Open the sample compartment lid
3. Align the module with the slot and press firmly until it clicks into
   place
4. The Trilogy will automatically detect the installed module and display
   the corresponding menu on the touch screen
5. If using the absorbance module, install the appropriate filter paddle
   for the target wavelength

### 6.3 Selecting the Measurement Mode

Each module offers two measurement modes:

| Mode                      | When to Use                                |
|:--------------------------|:-------------------------------------------|
| **Raw mode**              | Qualitative measurements, tracking relative changes. No calibration required. Results in RFU (fluorescence), raw absorbance, or NTU (turbidity). |
| **Direct Concentration mode** | Quantitative measurements requiring calibrated output in concentration units. Calibration required (see Section 7). |

Touch **Mode** on the home screen to toggle between modes.

### 6.4 Fluorescence Module: Chlorophyll *a* (EPA 445.0)

EPA Method 445.0 is the standard method for measuring extracted
chlorophyll *a* and pheophytin *a* in marine and freshwater algae by
fluorescence. It requires extraction with 90% acetone and measurements
before and after acidification.

1. Calibrate the fluorescence module in Direct Concentration mode using
   a known concentration of pure chlorophyll *a* in 90% acetone (see
   Section 7.3)
2. Insert the glass test tube containing the extracted sample
3. Touch **Measure Fluorescence** to obtain the pre-acidification
   reading
4. Add the prescribed volume of 0.1 N HCl, mix gently, and wait
   90 seconds
5. Measure again to obtain the post-acidification reading
6. Calculate chlorophyll *a* and pheophytin *a* concentrations per
   EPA 445.0

::: {.callout-tip}
### Tip
For greatest accuracy, recalibrate with a fresh chlorophyll *a* standard
every few months. The standard degrades over time, especially if exposed
to light or warmth.
:::

### 6.5 Single-Sample Measurements

1. Open the lid and insert the appropriate cuvette or test tube
2. Close the lid
3. Optionally, touch **Sample ID** to name the sample using the on-screen
   keypad; touch **Save**
4. Touch the **Measure** button corresponding to the installed module
   (Measure Fluorescence, Measure Absorbance, or Measure Turbidity)
5. The Trilogy measures the sample for 6 seconds and reports the average
   reading
6. Results for the most recent 20 measurements are displayed on the home
   screen; use the arrow keys to scroll through them

::: {.callout-important}
The Trilogy stores a maximum of 20 measurements at one time. Older
readings are overwritten. Measurements are not retained between power
cycles. Always export data to a printer or PC before turning off the
instrument or exceeding 20 readings.
:::

### 6.6 Continuous Sampling

1. Touch **Continuous Sampling** on the home screen and turn the feature
   **ON**
2. Set the measurement frequency and the total number of measurements
   (maximum 9,999)
3. Touch **OK** to return to the home screen
4. Connect the Trilogy to a printer or PC to capture all data
5. Do not touch the screen repeatedly during continuous sampling, as
   this will abort the measurement sequence

### 6.7 Shutdown

1. Export all data to a printer or PC
2. Remove the cuvette or test tube from the sample compartment
3. Clean the cuvette holder if any liquid was spilled (wipe with 70%
   ethanol and a lint-free tissue)
4. Close the sample compartment lid
5. Turn off the instrument using the rear power switch


## 7. Quality Control and Acceptance Criteria

### 7.1 When to Calibrate

1. Before running a new batch of samples (for greatest accuracy)
2. After a temperature change of +/- 5 C in the lab
3. After changing to a different optical module or switching to a
   different analyte
4. When verification readings on a known standard deviate unacceptably
   from the expected value

### 7.2 Calibration Overview

Calibration converts the raw instrument signal to concentration units.
The Trilogy supports single-point and multi-point calibrations (up to
five standards plus a blank). Multi-point calibrations generate a
calibration curve and provide superior accuracy across a wide
concentration range.

### 7.3 Direct Concentration Calibration Procedure

This procedure applies to all fluorescence and turbidity modules
(except the chlorophyll acidification and non-acidification modules,
which have their own dedicated procedures in the Trilogy manual).

1. Turn on the Trilogy and confirm the correct module is installed
2. Touch **Calibrate** on the home screen
3. Select **Run New Calibration**
4. Select the desired unit of measurement
5. Insert the blank (ultrapure water or 90% acetone, as appropriate)
   and touch **OK**
6. Enter the concentration of the first standard. For multi-point
   calibrations, begin with the lowest concentration and proceed in
   order of increasing concentration.
7. Insert the standard and touch **OK**
8. After the reading, either select **Proceed with Current Calibration**
   or **Enter More Standards** to add additional points
9. Optionally, save the calibration for future use
10. Verify the calibration by measuring the same standard used in step 6.
    The displayed concentration should match the known value within the
    acceptable tolerance for the application.

### 7.4 Verification

- After calibration, re-read a mid-range standard to confirm accuracy
- Re-read the standard every few hours during extended analytical
  sessions to detect drift
- Optionally, read the solid secondary standard and record its value
  for future instrument stability checks
- If the verification reading drifts beyond acceptable limits,
  recalibrate before continuing


## 8. Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                    | Disposal Method                          |
|:------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Acetone extracts              | Collect in organic waste carboy in fume hood; EH&S pickup |
| Acidified samples (HCl)       | Neutralize and dispose per [SOP-L003](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd) |
| Used cuvettes (non-hazardous) | Standard trash (polystyrene, methacrylate) or recycle (glass) |
| Formazine standards           | Collect in aqueous waste; EH&S pickup    |

## 10. Training Record

Before operating the Trilogy Fluorometer independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Complete [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd)
   training
3. Review the Turner Designs Trilogy User's Manual
4. Observe a trained operator perform module installation, calibration,
   and sample measurement
5. Perform a calibration and measure a set of standards with acceptable
   results under supervision
6. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager


## Appendix A: Troubleshooting -- Fluorescence {.appendix}

| Symptom                       | Probable Cause                  | Corrective Action              |
|:------------------------------|:--------------------------------|:-------------------------------|
| "Bad Calibration" error       | Blank brighter than standard    | Compare blank and standard in Raw mode; ensure standard is more concentrated than blank |
| Erratic readings              | Incorrect standard value entered during calibration | Review the standard value entered; it must match the actual standard concentration |
| Negative values               | Sample reading less than blank  | Normal if sample concentration is near zero; the blank value is automatically subtracted |
| Low readings                  | Wrong optical module for analyte | Verify that the excitation and emission wavelengths of the module match the analyte |
| High background signal        | Contaminated cuvette holder     | Clean the holder with 70% ethanol and a lint-free tissue |


## Appendix B: Troubleshooting -- Absorbance {.appendix}

| Symptom                       | Probable Cause                  | Corrective Action              |
|:------------------------------|:--------------------------------|:-------------------------------|
| Non-linear response           | Assay chemistry produces sigmoidal curve | Expected for some assays; use multi-point calibration |
| Low readings                  | Wrong filter paddle installed   | Check filter wavelength against assay requirements |
| "Bad Calibration" error       | Wrong filter or dirty blank     | Install correct filter; use ultrapure water in a clean cuvette to update the zero |


## Appendix C: Troubleshooting -- Turbidity {.appendix}

| Symptom                       | Probable Cause                  | Corrective Action              |
|:------------------------------|:--------------------------------|:-------------------------------|
| Readings disagree with other meters | Other meter uses visible light, not IR | Calibrate both with the same standard; color interference affects visible-light meters but not the Trilogy |
| Readings vary between replicates | Particle movement in sample    | Normal; particles shift position and scatter light differently each time |
| Readings change after recalibration with new standard | Formazine standard has aged | Use fresh formazine (valid for 4 weeks per ISO 7027) |
